name: Orbital Fold
lines: The Orbital: Meridian Ring · press E to dock and go aboard
The Orbital. The Ring Line shuttle docks with a soft clunk and the airlock opens. Meridian Ring's gate is ahead, past the control tower; the airlock behind you undocks or takes the shuttle home.
Docked at the Orbital. Your ship is held in the docking cradle. Meridian Ring's gate is ahead, past the control tower; the airlock behind you takes you back out to your ship.
Undocked. The Orbital turns behind you, Meridian Ring's windows lit all round it, the Earth below. M opens the star chart.
🛰️ The docking airlock The Orbital is a station over Earth, in Open Space. Ships dock here, and the Space Corp's Ring Line shuttle calls on the timetable.
back out to the ring, the Earth and the stars

🛰️ The docking airlock · press E to undock, or take the Ring Line shuttle

The Orbital is not behind a door any more: it is a station over Earth, in Open Space. Take the Ring Line shuttle from Launch Pad 1 at the Space Corp Spaceport, or fly your own ship up to the ring and dock. Meridian Ring, its homes, shops and the Academy of Flight are all there as before.
The Orbital is a ring station: it spins so that the floor of Meridian Ring pushes up on your feet, as a fairground ride pins you to its wall. That push stands in for gravity.
A ring 180 metres across has to turn about once every 19 seconds to give a full Earth weight at the rim. The idea goes back to Konstantin Tsiolkovsky in 1903, and Wernher von Braun drew one in 1952.
Like the real space station, the Orbital goes round the Earth about once every 92 minutes: sixteen sunrises a day.
🛰️ The Orbital is in Open Space now · by the Ring Line shuttle from the Spaceport
